newsitem.title: USA: Ill. bill would exempt rec bonds from state taxes.
newsitem.headline: Ill. bill would exempt rec bonds from state taxes.

text.p: CHICAGO, March 14 (Retuer) - A bill pending before an Illinois House committee would exempt local government bonds issued for recreational purposes from state income taxes.
State Rep. Duane Noland, R-Decatur, the bill's sponsor, said Friday the measure was aimed at making municipalities' small bond issues more attractive to potential buyers.
The bill would cover bonds or notes sold to finance recreational projects such as swimming pools, tennis courts, skating rinks and golf courses.
While Noland said he originally wanted to apply the bill to municipalities with populations of 25,000 or less, the bill contains no limit due to constitutional concerns.

Noland said the House Revenue Committee's subcommittee on income taxes was scheduled to hold a hearing on the bill next week. He said the Illinois Department of Revenue is expected to oppose the measure because of potential loss of state income tax revenues.

Noland acknowledged that municipalities could issue double-tax-exempt debt through the Illinois Rural Bond Bank or through the Illinois Development Finance Authority. However, he said those agencies tend to shun smaller bond issues and require "a lot of red tape."
He said allowing municipalities to issue their own bonds free of state income taxes would allow their residents to invest in the projects.
